items.prompt: Contoso has one Microsoft Entra tenant and three Azure subscriptions. A new team needs separate Azure billing and resource quotas but must keep using the existing Contoso identities. What should the administrator create?
constraints: Keep the existing identity directory.
Create a separate billing and quota boundary.
Do not introduce another authentication-policy boundary.

options.text: A new Azure subscription associated with the existing tenant.
A new Microsoft Entra tenant without a subscription.
A new resource group in an existing subscription.
A new management group containing the current subscriptions.

feedback.Reason: An Azure subscription is the resource, quota, and billing boundary; its associated Microsoft Entra tenant supplies the identities used for authorization.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Subscriptions trust principals from an associated tenant while retaining their own Azure resource and commercial boundaries.
Details.scenarioApplication: Create the team subscription under the current tenant and assign existing users or groups at the required scopes.
Details.errorCorrection: A new tenant changes identity ownership, while resource groups and management groups do not create subscription quotas.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Directory policies remain shared because the subscription still uses the existing tenant.
Details.transfer: Choose a separate tenant only when directory administration or authentication policy must also be independent.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A tenant separates identity administration but does not itself create the requested Azure resource and quota boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A resource group is a lifecycle container and does not provide independent subscription quotas or billing.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A management group scopes inherited governance but does not create a new billing or quota boundary.

items.prompt: Fabrikam must administer its own users, authentication methods, and external-collaboration settings without Contoso directory administrators changing them. Which boundary is required?
constraints: Directory administrators must be independent.
Authentication policies must be isolated.
Azure billing arrangements may be handled separately.

options.text: A resource group in the Contoso subscription.
A separate Microsoft Entra tenant for Fabrikam.
A management group in the Contoso tenant.
A security group containing Fabrikam users.

feedback.Reason: Independent directory administration and identity policy require a separate Microsoft Entra tenant.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A tenant owns users, groups, applications, directory roles, and tenant-level identity configuration.
Details.scenarioApplication: Provision Fabrikam in its own tenant and design cross-tenant collaboration explicitly.
Details.errorCorrection: Azure resource scopes and groups do not isolate tenant-level directory ownership.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A second tenant increases cross-tenant governance work but supplies the required identity separation.
Details.transfer: Use subscriptions or management groups when only Azure resource governance must differ.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.A: A resource group cannot isolate tenant-level identities or authentication settings.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A management group organizes Azure subscriptions but does not create a new directory.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A group remains inside one tenant and under that tenant's directory administration.

items.prompt: A SaaS application is registered in its publisher's tenant. Contoso consents to the app and wants to assign Contoso groups to it. Which Contoso object receives those tenant-local assignments?
constraints: The publisher retains the application definition.
Contoso needs a local security principal.
Assignments must be owned in the Contoso tenant.

options.text: The publisher tenant's Azure subscription.
A duplicate human user account.
The application's service principal in the Contoso tenant.
A management group named after the application.

feedback.Reason: A service principal is the local representation of an application in a Microsoft Entra tenant.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The application object defines the software, while each consuming tenant uses a service principal as its security principal.
Details.scenarioApplication: Assign Contoso users or groups to the Contoso service principal rather than changing the publisher's application object.
Details.errorCorrection: Subscriptions, users, and management groups do not provide the tenant-local application identity.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Deleting Contoso's service principal removes its local enterprise application but not the publisher's registration.
Details.transfer: For an Azure-hosted workload that only needs service authentication, evaluate managed identity.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.A: A subscription is an Azure resource scope, not the application's local identity in Contoso.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A user is the wrong identity type for representing an application.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A management group scopes Azure governance and cannot represent an application identity.

items.prompt: An Azure VM must retrieve Key Vault secrets. Policy forbids storing a client secret or certificate on the VM, and Azure must manage credential rotation. Which identity should be used?
constraints: Store no application credential on the VM.
Tie identity lifecycle to the VM.
Grant only the required Key Vault access.

options.text: A shared user with a non-expiring password.
A system-assigned managed identity on the VM.
The VM subscription ID used as a token.
A resource lock on the Key Vault.

feedback.Reason: Managed identity provides an Entra principal to an Azure resource without administrator-managed credentials.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A system-assigned identity is created for one resource and Azure manages token-signing credentials.
Details.scenarioApplication: Enable the VM identity and assign it the narrow Key Vault data role required by the workload.
Details.errorCorrection: Passwords, subscription IDs, and locks do not meet the service-authentication requirement.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Managed identity removes credential handling but does not grant permissions automatically.
Details.transfer: Use a user-assigned managed identity when several resources must share an independent identity lifecycle.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.A: This introduces a human credential and manual secret lifecycle, violating policy.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A subscription ID identifies a scope and is not an authentication credential.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A lock restricts management operations and does not authenticate the workload.

items.prompt: A partner employee must access one Contoso application with credentials managed by the partner. Contoso needs a local object for group assignment and later access review. What should Contoso create?
constraints: Do not issue a shared Contoso password.
Represent the person in Contoso's directory.
Keep application authorization under Contoso control.

options.text: A B2B collaboration guest user in Contoso's tenant.
An Azure resource group for the partner.
A managed identity assigned to the partner's browser.
A new Contoso tenant containing only the application.

feedback.Reason: B2B collaboration creates a tenant-local guest object while allowing the external user to authenticate with an external identity.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The guest receives a Contoso object ID and can join groups or receive application assignments after redemption.
Details.scenarioApplication: Invite the partner, verify redemption, and assign only the required application access.
Details.errorCorrection: Resource groups and managed identities are not external human identities, and another tenant is unnecessary.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Invitation redemption establishes identity presence but grants no application or Azure resource access by itself.
Details.transfer: Use an application trust rather than a guest user when the external actor is software, not a person.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A resource group cannot represent or authenticate a person.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Managed identities represent supported Azure resources, not external human users.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A new tenant is broader than the requested collaboration relationship.

items.prompt: A legacy server workload requires LDAP, Kerberos, computer domain join, and Group Policy. The company currently uses Microsoft Entra ID for cloud sign-in. Which conclusion is correct?
constraints: All four classic domain capabilities are mandatory.
Do not equate similar identity terminology with equivalent protocols.
Choose a supported directory boundary.

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID alone supplies all required AD DS protocols.
Azure RBAC on the servers supplies LDAP and Group Policy.
A management group supplies the domain hierarchy.
The workload requires AD DS or a supported managed domain service in addition to the Entra design.

feedback.Reason: Microsoft Entra ID is a cloud identity service; LDAP, Kerberos domain join, and Group Policy are classic AD DS domain capabilities.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Entra ID and AD DS differ in protocols, object management, and trust model even when identities are synchronized.
Details.scenarioApplication: Keep Entra for cloud identity and add an appropriate domain service for the legacy workload.
Details.errorCorrection: Azure RBAC and management groups are governance mechanisms, not directory protocol services.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Adding domain services introduces network, DNS, domain lifecycle, and synchronization work.
Details.transfer: For modern OAuth, OIDC, or SAML applications, prefer Entra integration instead of introducing AD DS by habit.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.A: Cloud directory membership does not provide classic AD DS LDAP, domain join, and Group Policy.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Azure RBAC authorizes Azure resource operations and is not a Windows domain service.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Management groups organize subscriptions and provide no directory protocols.

items.prompt: A daemon running outside Azure must call an Azure API without a signed-in user. Which sequence correctly establishes its identity and authorization?
constraints: The host cannot use Azure managed identity.
Authentication is application-only.
The principal must exist before authorization is assigned.

options.text: Create an app registration and tenant service principal, configure a protected credential or federation, then grant the principal only required access.
Assign RBAC to the application display name before creating its identity.
Create a resource lock and use the lock ID as a credential.
Create a new user for every run and embed its password.

feedback.Reason: A noninteractive application needs an application definition, tenant-local service principal, authentication method, and separate authorization.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The registration defines the client; the service principal is authorized; a credential or federation proves the application's identity.
Details.scenarioApplication: Create the identity artifacts, secure the authentication method, then assign only the required API or Azure role.
Details.errorCorrection: RBAC cannot target a nonexistent principal, locks are not identities, and human passwords are inappropriate.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Client secrets require rotation; certificates or workload federation can reduce secret risk when supported.
Details.transfer: Prefer managed identity when the workload later moves to a supported Azure hosting service.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: RBAC needs an existing, unambiguous security principal.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Resource locks do not create identities or credentials.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Human passwords are the wrong application-only credential model and violate secret protection.

items.prompt: An App Service app will read blobs with a system-assigned managed identity. Which implementation sequence is correct?
constraints: Store no account key or client secret.
Grant blob read access only.
Create the principal before its role assignment.

options.text: Assign a role to the app name, then enable identity only if access fails.
Enable identity, capture its principal ID, assign Storage Blob Data Reader at the required scope, then request a managed-identity token.
Enable identity and assume it automatically becomes subscription Owner.
Enable identity and make the container anonymous instead of assigning RBAC.

feedback.Reason: The managed identity principal must exist before RBAC can authorize it, and enabling identity alone grants no data access.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A system-assigned identity creates an Entra service principal tied to the App Service resource.
Details.scenarioApplication: Enable identity first, assign Storage Blob Data Reader at container or account scope, and use token authentication.
Details.errorCorrection: Display-name targeting, assumed Owner rights, and anonymous access violate the identity and authorization model.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Deleting the app deletes its system-assigned identity and leaves its former principal unusable.
Details.transfer: Use a user-assigned identity when the identity must survive replacement of the App Service resource.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.A: The principal ID does not exist until managed identity is enabled, and name matching is ambiguous.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Managed identity creates a principal but grants no permissions automatically.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Anonymous access defeats the identity-based least-privilege requirement.

items.prompt: A Microsoft Graph script signs in successfully, but lookup by a known user object ID returns resource not found. The object is visible in another organization's Entra admin center. What should be checked first?
constraints: The object ID was copied exactly.
Authentication succeeded.
The object exists in another tenant.

options.text: Whether the script authenticated to the tenant that owns the object.
Whether the user has an Azure cost budget.
Whether a subscription has a CanNotDelete lock.
Whether the display name follows storage-account naming rules.

feedback.Reason: A directory object ID is resolved inside a specific tenant; the correct ID queried against another tenant produces a not-found result.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Microsoft Graph requests run in the authenticated tenant context unless a supported cross-tenant operation is explicitly used.
Details.scenarioApplication: Inspect the token tenant ID, reconnect to the owning tenant, and repeat the exact-ID lookup.
Details.errorCorrection: Budgets, locks, and storage naming cannot alter Graph's directory context.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The same person may have separate objects and object IDs in different tenants.
Details.transfer: For RBAC troubleshooting, confirm that a role assignment uses the principal object from the subscription's associated tenant.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Budgets do not affect Graph directory-object resolution.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Azure resource locks do not control Graph directory lookup.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Storage naming rules are unrelated to Entra user lookup.

items.prompt: A user's UPN changes from alex@old.contoso.com to alex@contoso.com. Automation targeting the old UPN now fails, but the existing account and memberships must be preserved. Which identifier should the job use?
constraints: Update the existing object.
The sign-in name changed.
Do not create a replacement account.

options.text: The current display name.
The user's Azure subscription ID.
The user's Microsoft Entra object ID.
The object ID of the user's primary group.

feedback.Reason: The object ID is the stable key for the user object; UPN and display name are mutable properties.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Changing a UPN updates a property on the same directory object and does not create a new object ID.
Details.scenarioApplication: Persist or resolve the exact user object ID and target the update by that ID.
Details.errorCorrection: Names, subscription IDs, and group IDs do not durably identify the user object.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Object IDs are tenant-specific; a guest representation of the same person has another object ID.
Details.transfer: Use immutable IDs for role assignments and automation joins when readable identifiers can be renamed or reused.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.A: Display names are mutable and not guaranteed unique.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A subscription ID identifies an Azure resource boundary, not a user.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: That ID targets the group rather than the user to update.

items.prompt: An administrator must update a governed department attribute for 4,000 Entra users from CSV, record every failure, and rerun only failed rows. Which approach is most appropriate?
constraints: This is a directory data change, not an Azure resource deployment.
Record per-user results.
Make the process repeatable.

options.text: Use Microsoft Graph PowerShell or Graph API with exact IDs, input validation, and per-request error logging.
Declare all users in an ARM template.
Use AzCopy sync between the CSV and tenant.
Use Azure Policy remediation to modify user departments.

feedback.Reason: Microsoft Graph is the correct automation surface for Entra directory objects; ARM, AzCopy, and Azure Policy operate on different planes.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Graph calls can target exact object IDs and return operation-specific success or failure information.
Details.scenarioApplication: Validate input, process within throttling limits, log each result, and construct a retry set from failed rows.
Details.errorCorrection: ARM and Policy target Resource Manager resources; AzCopy targets storage data.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Bulk automation must handle throttling, partial failure, authorization, and idempotent retry.
Details.transfer: Use the admin center for a small inspected change when scale and repeatability are not required.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: ARM templates manage Azure resources, not Entra user profiles.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: AzCopy transfers storage data and cannot update directory users.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Azure Policy evaluates Azure resources, not Entra user properties.

items.prompt: One operator can reset Entra user passwords but cannot restart a VM. Another can restart the VM but cannot reset passwords. Both assignments are intentional. Which explanation is correct?
constraints: Do not broaden either operator's access.
Identify both authorization planes.
Treat successful sign-in separately from operation authorization.

options.text: Entra directory roles and Azure RBAC roles authorize different administrative planes.
Every Entra role automatically maps to an equivalent Azure role.
VM restart requires a Microsoft 365 license instead of RBAC.
Password reset is authorized by a VM resource lock.

feedback.Reason: Entra roles govern directory administration; Azure RBAC governs Azure resource operations at Azure scopes.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Each authorization system evaluates its own role definitions, principals, and scopes for a different plane.
Details.scenarioApplication: Keep the directory help-desk role and VM operator role separate because each already matches its duty.
Details.errorCorrection: Licenses and locks do not bridge the role systems, and similar role names do not imply equivalent permissions.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A portal may display both planes, but the underlying authorization checks remain separate.
Details.transfer: Before selecting a role, identify whether the target is a directory object, Azure resource, or service data.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: No general automatic permission mapping exists between the two role systems.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Product licensing does not grant Azure compute management actions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Locks constrain resource changes and do not grant directory permissions.

items.prompt: An engineer can create a storage account but receives authorization failure when listing blobs with Entra authentication. Which boundary explains the result?
constraints: Storage account creation succeeded.
Anonymous access and account keys are prohibited.
Blob listing uses the engineer's Entra identity.

options.text: Account creation is control-plane; blob listing is data-plane and needs a storage data role.
A tenant may contain users or Azure resources, but never both.
A subscription permits creation only after every blob is public.
The user must be converted into a service principal.

feedback.Reason: Resource Manager permission can authorize storage-account management without authorizing access to blob contents.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Role definitions distinguish management actions from service data actions, and Storage supplies blob data roles.
Details.scenarioApplication: Keep the management assignment and add Storage Blob Data Reader at the narrowest required scope.
Details.errorCorrection: Tenant composition, public access, and identity-type conversion do not explain the plane-specific result.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Granting data access exposes stored content and should not be implied by generic resource visibility.
Details.transfer: Apply the same plane distinction to Key Vault secrets, queues, tables, and other service data.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Tenants supply identities used to authorize resources; these concepts are not mutually exclusive.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Public blob access is unrelated to storage-account resource creation.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A user can receive a storage data role; identity-type conversion is not the missing permission.

items.prompt: An architect places two subscriptions under separate management groups and claims this guarantees a different Entra user directory for each subscription. Is the claim correct?
constraints: Both subscriptions currently trust one tenant.
Management groups may carry Policy and RBAC assignments.
The requirement is a separate user directory.

options.text: Yes; each management group creates a child Entra tenant.
Yes; management-group Policy duplicates every user into a new directory.
No; management groups separate inherited Azure governance, while a separate directory requires another tenant and explicit subscription association.
No; subscriptions cannot be organized under management groups.

feedback.Reason: Management groups are governance scopes above subscriptions; Microsoft Entra tenants are separate identity-directory boundaries.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A management-group tree scopes inherited Azure Policy and RBAC to descendant subscriptions in a tenant.
Details.scenarioApplication: Use management groups for governance, but create another tenant when directory ownership must be independent.
Details.errorCorrection: Management groups and Policy do not clone a directory, and subscriptions can be organized below management groups.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Moving a subscription in the hierarchy changes inherited governance, not the tenant directory by itself.
Details.transfer: Verify tenant association directly; do not infer identity boundaries from resource hierarchy names.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.A: Management groups do not create or own child tenants.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Azure Policy evaluates Azure resources and does not create tenant directories.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Subscriptions are the child resource type organized beneath management groups.
